answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance emerges when each participant must continuously prove unique resource commitments that flow like a river of ongoing attestations. New identities face a tundra of sparse initial interactions where reputation accrues slowly only through costly unique actions, and only after crossing a threshold do they enter a meadow of high-trust peers. Attackers must burn real compute or capital across many parallel identities for extended periods before any single one gains influence, making mass creation economically prohibitive.
